=== Truc Duel ===

Two players. The pack has 32 cards: 4 cards of each of 8 ranks; suits do not matter. Rank strength from highest to lowest: 7 (8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Both players start at 0 points.

Each round:
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and 3 cards are dealt privately to each player. Each player sees only their own hand.
2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). If a player's answer is invalid, their two cards are played in the order they were dealt. Trick 2 compares each player's first card; trick 3 compares each player's second card. In each trick, higher strength wins and equal strength is spoilt.
5. Round winner. The player who won more of the three tricks wins the round. If both won the same number, the winner of the earliest trick that was not spoilt wins the round. If all three tricks were spoilt, the round is void and no one scores.
6. Scoring. The round winner adds the round's value (1, 2 or 4) to their score; the other player's score is unchanged.
7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

If 30 rounds have been played and no one has reached 12, the game ends: the higher score wins, and equal scores are a draw (a shared win). There is no talk phase: all information comes from revealed cards and choices.

Two players. The pack has 32 cards: 4 cards of each of 8 ranks; suits do not matter. Rank strength from highest to lowest: 7 (8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Both players start at 0 points.

Each round:
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and 3 cards are dealt privately to each player. Each player sees only their own hand.
2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). If a player's answer is invalid, their two cards are played in the order they were dealt. Trick 2 compares each player's first card; trick 3 compares each player's second card. In each trick, higher strength wins and equal strength is spoilt.
5. Round winner. The player who won more of the three tricks wins the round. If both won the same number, the winner of the earliest trick that was not spoilt wins the round. If all three tricks were spoilt, the round is void and no one scores.
6. Scoring. The round winner adds the round's value (1, 2 or 4) to their score; the other player's score is unchanged.
7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

If 30 rounds have been played and no one has reached 12, the game ends: the higher score wins, and equal scores are a draw (a shared win). There is no talk phase: all information comes from revealed cards and choices.

Each round:
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and 3 cards are dealt privately to each player. Each player sees only their own hand.
2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). 7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

=== Truc Duel ===

Two players. The pack has 32 cards: 4 cards of each of 8 ranks; suits do not matter. Rank strength from highest to lowest: 7 (8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Both players start at 0 points.

Each round:
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and 3 cards are dealt privately to each player. Each player sees only their own hand.
2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). If a player's answer is invalid, their two cards are played in the order they were dealt. Trick 2 compares each player's first card; trick 3 compares each player's second card. In each trick, higher strength wins and equal strength is spoilt.
5. Round winner. The player who won more of the three tricks wins the round. If both won the same number, the winner of the earliest trick that was not spoilt wins the round. If all three tricks were spoilt, the round is void and no one scores.
6. Scoring. The round winner adds the round's value (1, 2 or 4) to their score; the other player's score is unchanged.
7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

If 30 rounds have been played and no one has reached 12, the game ends: the higher score wins, and equal scores are a draw (a shared win). There is no talk phase: all information comes from revealed cards and choices.

[user]
=== Truc Duel ===

Two players. The pack has 32 cards: 4 cards of each of 8 ranks; suits do not matter. Rank strength from highest to lowest: 7 (8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Both players start at 0 points.

Each round:
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and 3 cards are dealt privately to each player. Each player sees only their own hand.
2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). If a player's answer is invalid, their two cards are played in the order they were dealt. Trick 2 compares each player's first card; trick 3 compares each player's second card. In each trick, higher strength wins and equal strength is spoilt.
5. Round winner. The player who won more of the three tricks wins the round. If both won the same number, the winner of the earliest trick that was not spoilt wins the round. If all three tricks were spoilt, the round is void and no one scores.
6. Scoring. The round winner adds the round's value (1, 2 or 4) to their score; the other player's score is unchanged.
7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

If 30 rounds have been played and no one has reached 12, the game ends: the higher score wins, and equal scores are a draw (a shared win). There is no talk phase: all information comes from revealed cards and choices.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

Rank order, highest first: 7 (strength 8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Stakes: both STAY 1 point; ACCEPT 2; FOUR 4; both TWO MORE 4; a FOLD gives the raiser 1. First to 12 wins.

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

[user]
=== Truc Duel ===

Two players. The pack has 32 cards: 4 cards of each of 8 ranks; suits do not matter. Rank strength from highest to lowest: 7 (8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Both players start at 0 points.

Each round:
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and 3 cards are dealt privately to each player. Each player sees only their own hand.
2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). If a player's answer is invalid, their two cards are played in the order they were dealt. Trick 2 compares each player's first card; trick 3 compares each player's second card. In each trick, higher strength wins and equal strength is spoilt.
5. Round winner. The player who won more of the three tricks wins the round. If both won the same number, the winner of the earliest trick that was not spoilt wins the round. If all three tricks were spoilt, the round is void and no one scores.
6. Scoring. The round winner adds the round's value (1, 2 or 4) to their score; the other player's score is unchanged.
7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

If 30 rounds have been played and no one has reached 12, the game ends: the higher score wins, and equal scores are a draw (a shared win). There is no talk phase: all information comes from revealed cards and choices.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Rank order, highest first: 7 (strength 8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Stakes: both STAY 1 point; ACCEPT 2; FOUR 4; both TWO MORE 4; a FOLD gives the raiser 1. First to 12 wins.

Each round runs in this order: new round → deal → your hand → first trick → resolve trick 1 → trick 1 revealed → raise poll → settle the raise → response → apply the response → order of last two cards → tricks 2 and 3 → round result → end check.

Actions you may be asked for:
  first_trick  answer with one of the options you are given
  raise_poll   answer with one of: STAY, TWO MORE
  response     answer with one of: ACCEPT, FOLD, FOUR
  order_of_last_two_cards answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

[user]
=== Truc Duel ===

Two players. The pack has 32 cards: 4 cards of each of 8 ranks; suits do not matter. Rank strength from highest to lowest: 7 (8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Both players start at 0 points.

Each round:
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and 3 cards are dealt privately to each player. Each player sees only their own hand.
2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). If a player's answer is invalid, their two cards are played in the order they were dealt. Trick 2 compares each player's first card; trick 3 compares each player's second card. In each trick, higher strength wins and equal strength is spoilt.
5. Round winner. The player who won more of the three tricks wins the round. If both won the same number, the winner of the earliest trick that was not spoilt wins the round. If all three tricks were spoilt, the round is void and no one scores.
6. Scoring. The round winner adds the round's value (1, 2 or 4) to their score; the other player's score is unchanged.
7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

If 30 rounds have been played and no one has reached 12, the game ends: the higher score wins, and equal scores are a draw (a shared win). There is no talk phase: all information comes from revealed cards and choices.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Rank order, highest first: 7 (strength 8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Stakes: both STAY 1 point; ACCEPT 2; FOUR 4; both TWO MORE 4; a FOLD gives the raiser 1. First to 12 wins.

Each round runs in this order: new round → deal → your hand → first trick → resolve trick 1 → trick 1 revealed → raise poll → settle the raise → response → apply the response → order of last two cards → tricks 2 and 3 → round result → end check.

Actions you may be asked for:
  first_trick  answer with one of the options you are given
  raise_poll   answer with one of: STAY, TWO MORE
  response     answer with one of: ACCEPT, FOLD, FOUR
  order_of_last_two_cards answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.

  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

[user]
=== Truc Duel ===

Two players. The pack has 32 cards: 4 cards of each of 8 ranks; suits do not matter. Rank strength from highest to lowest: 7 (8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Both players start at 0 points.

Each round:
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and 3 cards are dealt privately to each player. Each player sees only their own hand.
2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). If a player's answer is invalid, their two cards are played in the order they were dealt. Trick 2 compares each player's first card; trick 3 compares each player's second card. In each trick, higher strength wins and equal strength is spoilt.
5. Round winner. The player who won more of the three tricks wins the round. If both won the same number, the winner of the earliest trick that was not spoilt wins the round. If all three tricks were spoilt, the round is void and no one scores.
6. Scoring. The round winner adds the round's value (1, 2 or 4) to their score; the other player's score is unchanged.
7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

If 30 rounds have been played and no one has reached 12, the game ends: the higher score wins, and equal scores are a draw (a shared win). There is no talk phase: all information comes from revealed cards and choices.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Truc Duel ===

Two players. The pack has 32 cards: 4 cards of each of 8 ranks; suits do not matter. Rank strength from highest to lowest: 7 (8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Both players start at 0 points.

Each round:
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and 3 cards are dealt privately to each player. Each player sees only their own hand.
2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). If a player's answer is invalid, their two cards are played in the order they were dealt. Trick 2 compares each player's first card; trick 3 compares each player's second card. In each trick, higher strength wins and equal strength is spoilt.
5. Round winner. The player who won more of the three tricks wins the round. If both won the same number, the winner of the earliest trick that was not spoilt wins the round. If all three tricks were spoilt, the round is void and no one scores.
6. Scoring. The round winner adds the round's value (1, 2 or 4) to their score; the other player's score is unchanged.
7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

If 30 rounds have been played and no one has reached 12, the game ends: the higher score wins, and equal scores are a draw (a shared win). There is no talk phase: all information comes from revealed cards and choices.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Rank order, highest first: 7 (strength 8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Stakes: both STAY 1 point; ACCEPT 2; FOUR 4; both TWO MORE 4; a FOLD gives the raiser 1. First to 12 wins.

Each round runs in this order: new round → deal → your hand → first trick → resolve trick 1 → trick 1 revealed → raise poll → settle the raise → response → apply the response → order of last two cards → tricks 2 and 3 → round result → end check.

Actions you may be asked for:
  first_trick  answer with one of the options you are given
  raise_poll   answer with one of: STAY, TWO MORE
  response     answer with one of: ACCEPT, FOLD, FOUR
  order_of_last_two_cards answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Truc Duel ===

Two players. The pack has 32 cards: 4 cards of each of 8 ranks; suits do not matter. Rank strength from highest to lowest: 7 (8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Both players start at 0 points.

Each round:
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and 3 cards are dealt privately to each player. Each player sees only their own hand.
2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). 2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. 7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). If a player's answer is invalid, their two cards are played in the order they were dealt. Trick 2 compares each player's first card; trick 3 compares each player's second card. In each trick, higher strength wins and equal strength is spoilt.
5. Round winner. The player who won more of the three tricks wins the round. If both won the same number, the winner of the earliest trick that was not spoilt wins the round. If all three tricks were spoilt, the round is void and no one scores.
6. Scoring. The round winner adds the round's value (1, 2 or 4) to their score; the other player's score is unchanged.
7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Truc Duel ===

Two players. The pack has 32 cards: 4 cards of each of 8 ranks; suits do not matter. Rank strength from highest to lowest: 7 (8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Both players start at 0 points.

Each round:
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and 3 cards are dealt privately to each player. Each player sees only their own hand.
2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). If a player's answer is invalid, their two cards are played in the order they were dealt. Trick 2 compares each player's first card; trick 3 compares each player's second card. In each trick, higher strength wins and equal strength is spoilt.
5. Round winner. The player who won more of the three tricks wins the round. If both won the same number, the winner of the earliest trick that was not spoilt wins the round. If all three tricks were spoilt, the round is void and no one scores.
6. Scoring. The round winner adds the round's value (1, 2 or 4) to their score; the other player's score is unchanged.
7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

If 30 rounds have been played and no one has reached 12, the game ends: the higher score wins, and equal scores are a draw (a shared win). There is no talk phase: all information comes from revealed cards and choices.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Rank order, highest first: 7 (strength 8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Stakes: both STAY 1 point; ACCEPT 2; FOUR 4; both TWO MORE 4; a FOLD gives the raiser 1. First to 12 wins.

Each round runs in this order: new round → deal → your hand → first trick → resolve trick 1 → trick 1 revealed → raise poll → settle the raise → response → apply the response → order of last two cards → tricks 2 and 3 → round result → end check.

Actions you may be asked for:
  first_trick  answer with one of the options you are given
  raise_poll   answer with one of: STAY, TWO MORE
  response     answer with one of: ACCEPT, FOLD, FOUR
  order_of_last_two_cards answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

Two players. The pack has 32 cards: 4 cards of each of 8 ranks; suits do not matter. Rank strength from highest to lowest: 7 (8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Both players start at 0 points.

Each round:
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and 3 cards are dealt privately to each player. Each player sees only their own hand.
2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). If a player's answer is invalid, their two cards are played in the order they were dealt. Trick 2 compares each player's first card; trick 3 compares each player's second card. In each trick, higher strength wins and equal strength is spoilt.
5. Round winner. The player who won more of the three tricks wins the round. If both won the same number, the winner of the earliest trick that was not spoilt wins the round. If all three tricks were spoilt, the round is void and no one scores.
6. Scoring. The round winner adds the round's value (1, 2 or 4) to their score; the other player's score is unchanged.
7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

If 30 rounds have been played and no one has reached 12, the game ends: the higher score wins, and equal scores are a draw (a shared win). There is no talk phase: all information comes from revealed cards and choices.

[user]
=== Truc Duel ===

Two players. The pack has 32 cards: 4 cards of each of 8 ranks; suits do not matter. Rank strength from highest to lowest: 7 (8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Both players start at 0 points.

Each round:
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and 3 cards are dealt privately to each player. Each player sees only their own hand.
2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). If a player's answer is invalid, their two cards are played in the order they were dealt. Trick 2 compares each player's first card; trick 3 compares each player's second card. In each trick, higher strength wins and equal strength is spoilt.
5. Round winner. The player who won more of the three tricks wins the round. If both won the same number, the winner of the earliest trick that was not spoilt wins the round. If all three tricks were spoilt, the round is void and no one scores.
6. Scoring. The round winner adds the round's value (1, 2 or 4) to their score; the other player's score is unchanged.
7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

If 30 rounds have been played and no one has reached 12, the game ends: the higher score wins, and equal scores are a draw (a shared win). There is no talk phase: all information comes from revealed cards and choices.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Rank order, highest first: 7 (strength 8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Stakes: both STAY 1 point; ACCEPT 2; FOUR 4; both TWO MORE 4; a FOLD gives the raiser 1. First to 12 wins.

Each round runs in this order: new round → deal → your hand → first trick → resolve trick 1 → trick 1 revealed → raise poll → settle the raise → response → apply the response → order of last two cards → tricks 2 and 3 → round result → end check.

Actions you may be asked for:
  first_trick  answer with one of the options you are given
  raise_poll   answer with one of: STAY, TWO MORE
  response     answer with one of: ACCEPT, FOLD, FOUR
  order_of_last_two_cards answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

Two players. The pack has 32 cards: 4 cards of each of 8 ranks; suits do not matter. Rank strength from highest to lowest: 7 (8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Both players start at 0 points.

Each round:
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and 3 cards are dealt privately to each player. Each player sees only their own hand.
2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). If a player's answer is invalid, their two cards are played in the order they were dealt. Trick 2 compares each player's first card; trick 3 compares each player's second card. In each trick, higher strength wins and equal strength is spoilt.
5. Round winner. The player who won more of the three tricks wins the round. If both won the same number, the winner of the earliest trick that was not spoilt wins the round. If all three tricks were spoilt, the round is void and no one scores.
6. Scoring. The round winner adds the round's value (1, 2 or 4) to their score; the other player's score is unchanged.
7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

If 30 rounds have been played and no one has reached 12, the game ends: the higher score wins, and equal scores are a draw (a shared win). There is no talk phase: all information comes from revealed cards and choices.

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.

Each round runs in this order: new round → deal → your hand → first trick → resolve trick 1 → trick 1 revealed → raise poll → settle the raise → response → apply the response → order of last two cards → tricks 2 and 3 → round result → end check.

Each round:
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and 3 cards are dealt privately to each player. Each player sees only their own hand.
2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). If a player's answer is invalid, their two cards are played in the order they were dealt. Trick 2 compares each player's first card; trick 3 compares each player's second card. In each trick, higher strength wins and equal strength is spoilt.
5. Round winner. The player who won more of the three tricks wins the round. If both won the same number, the winner of the earliest trick that was not spoilt wins the round. If all three tricks were spoilt, the round is void and no one scores.

7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

Two players. The pack has 32 cards: 4 cards of each of 8 ranks; suits do not matter. Rank strength from highest to lowest: 7 (8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Both players start at 0 points.

Each round:
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and 3 cards are dealt privately to each player. Each player sees only their own hand.
2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). If a player's answer is invalid, their two cards are played in the order they were dealt. Trick 2 compares each player's first card; trick 3 compares each player's second card. In each trick, higher strength wins and equal strength is spoilt.
5. Round winner. The player who won more of the three tricks wins the round. If both won the same number, the winner of the earliest trick that was not spoilt wins the round. If all three tricks were spoilt, the round is void and no one scores.
6. Scoring. The round winner adds the round's value (1, 2 or 4) to their score; the other player's score is unchanged.
7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

If 30 rounds have been played and no one has reached 12, the game ends: the higher score wins, and equal scores are a draw (a shared win). There is no talk phase: all information comes from revealed cards and choices.

Two players. The pack has 32 cards: 4 cards of each of 8 ranks; suits do not matter. Rank strength from highest to lowest: 7 (8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Both players start at 0 points.

2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.

7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

Two players. The pack has 32 cards: 4 cards of each of 8 ranks; suits do not matter. Rank strength from highest to lowest: 7 (8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Both players start at 0 points.

Each round:
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and 3 cards are dealt privately to each player. Each player sees only their own hand.
2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). If a player's answer is invalid, their two cards are played in the order they were dealt. Trick 2 compares each player's first card; trick 3 compares each player's second card. In each trick, higher strength wins and equal strength is spoilt.
5. Round winner. The player who won more of the three tricks wins the round. If both won the same number, the winner of the earliest trick that was not spoilt wins the round. If all three tricks were spoilt, the round is void and no one scores.
6. Scoring. The round winner adds the round's value (1, 2 or 4) to their score; the other player's score is unchanged.
7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

If 30 rounds have been played and no one has reached 12, the game ends: the higher score wins, and equal scores are a draw (a shared win). There is no talk phase: all information comes from revealed cards and choices.

records.system:
You are reviewing a game that has finished. You were not a player. You are shown everything: the messages the table was told, every move, and each player's private thinking at every move, which no other player ever saw. Each move carries the notes its game asked for, under their own names. The usual ones are:

  plan     what they meant to do over the coming turns
  reason   why they made that move
  predict  what they expected their opponents to do
  adjust   how they changed their own strategy because of that

Write two things.

First, a summary of the whole game as it unfolded: the turning points, the moves that decided it, and how it ended. Concrete: name seats, rounds and numbers.

Second, a review of each player. Judge their play, not their luck. For each one, compare their predictions with what their opponents were actually thinking and actually did: were they right, and did they see it in time? Did their adjustments follow from their predictions, and did their moves follow from their reasons? Point out their best and worst moves. Then score their play from 1 to 10, where 1 is aimless or self-defeating and 10 is sharp, well read and well executed. A player can lose and still score well, or win and score badly.

A player who gave no reasons, predictions or adjustments is judged on their moves alone; say that their thinking was not recorded.

Refer to each player by seat, and as "they".

THE GAME
Two players. The pack has 32 cards: 4 cards of each of 8 ranks; suits do not matter. Rank strength from highest to lowest: 7 (8), 8 (7), A (6), K (5), Q (4), J (3), 10 (2), 9 (1). Both players start at 0 points.

Each round:
1. Deal. The full pack is shuffled and 3 cards are dealt privately to each player. Each player sees only their own hand.
2. First trick. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose one card from their hand to play. If a player names a card not in their hand, their first-listed card is played. Both cards are revealed. The higher strength wins trick 1. Equal strength means trick 1 is spoilt and belongs to no one.
3. Raise poll. Both players secretly and simultaneously choose STAY or TWO MORE. The choices are then revealed. Both STAY: the round is worth 1 point. Both TWO MORE: the round is worth 4 points, and no one may fold. Exactly one TWO MORE: that player is the raiser. The other player, the responder, answers once with ACCEPT, FOLD or FOUR. ACCEPT: the round is worth 2 points. FOLD: the raiser immediately scores 1 point, the responder scores nothing, and the round ends (no more cards are played). FOUR: the round is worth 4 points, and the raiser may not fold.
4. Last two tricks. Each player secretly and simultaneously chooses the order in which they will play their two remaining cards (first, then second). If a player's answer is invalid, their two cards are played in the order they were dealt. Trick 2 compares each player's first card; trick 3 compares each player's second card. In each trick, higher strength wins and equal strength is spoilt.
5. Round winner. The player who won more of the three tricks wins the round. If both won the same number, the winner of the earliest trick that was not spoilt wins the round. If all three tricks were spoilt, the round is void and no one scores.
6. Scoring. The round winner adds the round's value (1, 2 or 4) to their score; the other player's score is unchanged.
7. End check. If a player has 12 or more points, the game ends and that player wins.

If 30 rounds have been played and no one has reached 12, the game ends: the higher score wins, and equal scores are a draw (a shared win). There is no talk phase: all information comes from revealed cards and choices.
